summary.text: CA9 is the candidate on which omics, literature, external knowledge, single-cell and spatial data agree most. It leads the overall convergence ranking, its tumour transcripts come from the cancer cells themselves rather than from stroma [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], and antibody and imaging agents based on girentuximab are already in clinical development. It is best read as a surface antigen and imaging biomarker, not as a dependency: no ccRCC cell line depends on it [gene=CA9; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0].

Behind CA9, the target profile is led by a small group whose position survives random re-weighting: SCARB1, CD70, NNMT, SLC16A3 and ENPP3. SCARB1 and NNMT also replicate at the protein level in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort, and CD70 and ENPP3 carry precedent from clinical antibodies or conjugates. None of them is a selective dependency in DepMap. Among the reviewed genes only EPAS1, the target of the approved HIF-2 alpha inhibitor belzutifan, shows a selective ccRCC dependency, so most candidates are antigen or biomarker cases rather than driver targets, and the established drug targets EPAS1, KDR and MTOR serve as reference points.

For biomarkers, the calls that hold under re-weighting are metabolic genes that fall in tumours. PSAT1 replicates as lower in tumours in the confirmatory cohort [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946], and so does PCK1 [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819]. ALDOB, UMOD and SLC22A8 mark the loss of proximal-tubule identity, and NNMT is the main tumour-up biomarker, with an adverse survival association in TCGA-KIRC. These are diagnostic or prognostic leads, not targets.

The convergence ranking rewards literature and existing drugs, so it cannot put a little-studied gene on top; the discovery screen is where such genes are found, and it identifies two tumour-cell candidates that are prioritised for experimental validation. COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, is made mainly by RCC cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. Its protein is higher in tumours [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; protein_log2fc=2.512], the rise replicates in TCGA [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.8291] and it survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]. Still missing are proof that the protein sits on the cell surface, staining in normal tissues, a selective dependency, confirmatory-cohort data and a measure of heterogeneity, since only a minority of RCC cells express it [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_pct=17.1%]. Immunohistochemistry on tumour and normal tissue arrays, followed by knockdown in ccRCC cell lines, would test it. RAB42, a small Rab GTPase, is also mostly in RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627], with higher tumour protein and TCGA replication [gene=RAB42; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.3712], but macrophages hold a sizeable share of its transcripts [gene=RAB42; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.1.share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.319] and the protein is intracellular, so a functional knockdown study fits it better than an antibody. The stroma track (OLFML2A, JAG2) and the immune track, which makes up most of the pool, give weaker tumour-cell hypotheses. Novel here means at most fifteen ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, not that nothing has been published; the literature agent did not examine these genes, and nothing in this analysis shows that treating them would help a patient.

omics.text: The CPTAC tumour-versus-normal data put a HIF-driven, tumour-up programme at the top. CA9, NNMT, SLC16A3, CD70, ENPP3 and SCARB1 are higher in tumour at both the RNA and protein layers, and each survives the purity check, so the signal is not an artefact of infiltration. The programme follows from loss of VHL, the dominant recurrent driver, mutated in close to half of patients [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.4834], whose 3p copy loss also has a real dosage effect on its RNA [gene=VHL; type=cis_dosage; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; rna_rho=0.506].

At the other end, the strongest down-regulated genes reflect loss of normal tubule identity. ALDOB RNA is very strongly down in tumour (log2FC -7.028), with protein and phospho also down, TCGA replication and an association between low expression and worse survival. UMOD and PSAT1 follow the same pattern. These genes are diagnostic or prognostic biomarker candidates, not targets.

literature.text: The literature stream supports the two leading surface antigens. CA9 is reported as enriched in ccRCC tumour cells with low background in normal kidney, and CA9-targeted PET is described as proof of concept that still needs prospective validation. CD70 is described as commonly overexpressed in renal cell carcinoma, minimally expressed in normal tissue and possibly a HIF target gene, and CD70-specific single-domain antibodies have been labelled as radiotracers. Both bodies of evidence are early: imaging and preclinical work rather than therapeutic trials.

COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) is reported as HIF-induced, overexpressed in most ccRCCs and a suppressor of mitochondrial ferroptosis, and a mouse model links it to CA9 expression, which ties the top two convergence genes into one hypoxia programme; the evidence is preclinical. NNMT is linked to worse survival in a study with transcriptomic and functional validation, and selective NNMT inhibitors exist, although that chemistry work is not ccRCC-specific. MT1G is contradictory, lower in tumour yet linked to poor prognosis and tumour promotion. SCARB1 and PIGR have no literature relations in this corpus despite strong data support.

external.text: Open Targets and DepMap separate established targets from antigen-type candidates. EPAS1 has a strong Open Targets association [gene=EPAS1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4871] and is the only reviewed gene with a selective ccRCC dependency [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3], in a minority of lines [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0.208]. MTOR is needed by every ccRCC line [gene=MTOR; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=1] but is common essential, a toxicity risk rather than selectivity. KDR has approved inhibitors yet no cell-line dependency [gene=KDR; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0], as expected for an anti-angiogenic target.

For the data-led candidates the external layer is weaker. CA9 has a moderate Open Targets association [gene=CA9; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3088] and is antibody-accessible at the membrane; CD70 has a weak prior association [gene=CD70; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.0572] but advanced antibody tractability. SCARB1 is supported mainly by genetic association [gene=SCARB1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.519] and has no drugs, and NNMT is small-molecule tractable without a clinical drug. None of the four shows a ccRCC dependency, so they are conjugate, cell-therapy or biomarker cases.

cells.text: Single-cell data confirm that CA9 is tumour-intrinsic. About half of RCC cells express it [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=54.7%], it is far higher in tumour cells than in donor-paired proximal tubule cells [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739], and the attribution to RCC cells holds in a second single-cell dataset [gene=CA9; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.981].

Several bulk candidates are not tumour-intrinsic. KDR is endothelial [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], CD74 is carried mostly by macrophages [gene=CD74; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436] and CXCR4 by CD8 T cells [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.563], so they are microenvironment genes. NNMT attribution to RCC cells holds in the second dataset [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.948], whereas SLC16A3 does not replicate: T and NK cells dominate in Li 2022 [gene=SLC16A3; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.327] but RCC cells in Zhang 2021, so its cell of origin is unresolved.

spatial.text: Visium sections place the two reference genes in different niches. The composition-corrected in-situ expresser of CA9 is RCC [gene=CA9; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; in_situ_expressers.0.composition_corrected_share=0.999], and its high-expression spots sit among other RCC spots [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381]. KDR is expressed in situ by endothelium [gene=KDR; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; in_situ_expressers.0.composition_corrected_share=0.99] with almost no tumour-cell contribution [gene=KDR; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; in_situ_expressers.1.composition_corrected_share=0.002], consistent with a vascular niche.

structure.text: The AlphaFold model of CA9 is of moderate confidence [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56], and its top computationally detected cavity in the predicted monomer has a moderate structural-context score [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.546]. The detected cavities cover part of the experimentally known ligand contacts [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]. These scores are descriptive heuristics; they are not evidence of a degron, of ligase compatibility or of a degrader, and no curated degron or ternary-complex reference applies to CA9 here.

For the discovery candidate COL23A1 the AlphaFold model is low confidence [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91] with only a tiny detected cavity, so an antibody against an extracellular domain is the more plausible modality than a small molecule or degrader.

discovery.text: Tumour track. COL23A1 is a transmembrane collagen with few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, and it leads the tumour-cell track because RCC cells make most of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. The rise replicates in TCGA-KIRC and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour, so it is not an infiltration effect. It carries no adverse survival signal [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.123]. Missing are dependency evidence, confirmation of the protein at the cell surface, normal-tissue staining and confirmatory-cohort data, and expression is restricted to a minority of RCC cells, so heterogeneity is the main open question.

RAB42 is a small Rab GTPase, the second tumour-track candidate. Few RCC cells express it [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_pct=11.6%]. Its protein is higher in tumours [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; protein_log2fc=1.898], and the change holds at full purity [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189]. It lacks functional or dependency evidence, it is intracellular rather than a surface protein, and part of its signal comes from macrophages.

Stroma track. OLFML2A is a secreted fibroblast gene [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647] that replicates in TCGA and holds at full purity, with an off-tumour concern from colon expression. JAG2, a Notch ligand, is mainly endothelial [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.487] and holds at full purity, but heart-muscle expression needs a safety assessment. Neither has a clinical drug or dependency evidence.

Immune track, which makes up most of the discovery pool. GAL3ST4 is a macrophage gene [gene=GAL3ST4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.972] whose higher expression goes with worse survival, but its bulk rise shrinks at full purity [gene=GAL3ST4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.401], so it reflects macrophage infiltration. MILR1 has no ccRCC papers but is flagged as infiltration-driven, and SLC37A2 is macrophage-held with only a small pure-tumour effect. These are hypotheses about the macrophage compartment, not tumour-cell targets, and none is a selective dependency.

validation.text: The confirmatory CPTAC cohort (DIA proteome) replicates the protein direction for NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776] and SCARB1 [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334], and for the tumour-down biomarkers PSAT1 and PCK1. HK2 does not replicate: its discovery increase [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_discovery_log2fc=2.106] is absent in the confirmatory cohort [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256], which weakens it as a target despite its place in the target profile.

External replication and the purity check strengthen the tumour-cell candidates. CD70 replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=CD70; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=7.0902] and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=CD70; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.278], as do CA9, NNMT, SCARB1 and the discovery candidate COL23A1, whereas CD74 falls as purity rises and GAL3ST4 nearly vanishes at full purity, marking them as infiltration. Among drivers, VHL and PBRM1 are recurrent [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362] but are tumour suppressors, so they are stratification markers. No candidate other than EPAS1 has a selective DepMap dependency, and protein-adjusted kinase activity did not contribute to any of the leading calls.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the evidence streams, a small set of calls is stable. In the target profile, SCARB1 [gene=SCARB1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=8], CA9 [gene=CA9; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.94], SLC16A3 [gene=SLC16A3; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.881] and NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top25=0.954], together with CD70 and ENPP3, stay near the top. In the biomarker profile, PSAT1 [gene=PSAT1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=5] and PCK1 [gene=PCK1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.881] are the robust calls.

Other positions depend on the chosen weights. PIGR can reach the top of the overall ranking but has a wide interval [gene=PIGR; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:convergence:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=convergence; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=56], and VHL swings from the top to far down the list [gene=VHL; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:convergence:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=convergence; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=590]. ALDOB, third overall, often leaves the biomarker top twenty-five once weights vary [gene=ALDOB; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.p_top25=0.469]. In the overall ranking only CA9 and COXFA4L2 are robust top-ten calls, so the overall score should not be read as a fixed ordering.

treatment.text: In IMmotion150, CA9 is not significantly associated with progression in any arm. Higher expression points towards longer benefit on sunitinib [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], but the adjusted p-value is not significant [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.padj=0.332], and the difference between arms is not significant either [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.78]. This is an association to follow up, not a predictor.

For EPAS1 and NNMT only the small Choueiri nivolumab trial returned a result, and neither association is significant [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_choueiri2016.padj=0.88] [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_choueiri2016.padj=0.782]. No examined gene separates the two main IMmotion150 arms after correction, and absence of an arm result is not evidence of no association.

subtypes.text: CA9 is flagged as a subgroup target candidate for PBRM1-mutant tumours. The flag is driven by RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.971], while the protein difference is modest and not significant [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_protein.padj=0.067]. CA9 is lower in ccB than ccA in all three cohorts.

PSAT1 and PCK1 are not subgroup candidates for VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2. Both interact with the ccA/ccB split, PSAT1 at protein and RNA and PCK1 at RNA only, so their biomarker value may differ between the two subtypes. Subtype differences in bulk data can partly reflect different immune and stromal content, so they need confirmation in purified tumour cells.

adc.text: Among known conjugate targets used as controls, CD70 has the highest suitability [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746], but no normal-tissue staining data were available, so its safety cannot be judged here. CA9 scores well [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647] and is absent from normal kidney, with strong stomach staining as a flag. ENPP3 [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.578] stains normal kidney and duodenum, an on-target toxicity concern. All three are patchy in the weakest donors, and a high score does not show that a conjugate or radioligand would work.

SCARB1 tops the target profile but is a weaker conjugate candidate, with strong adrenal and moderate kidney staining, and few tumour cells express it in the weakest donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%], so heterogeneity is a risk.

immune.text: A large part of CD70 tumour transcripts come from immune cells [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654], and it tracks CD8 T cells modestly, so its bulk RNA partly reflects infiltration and on-target expression in T cells must be considered for any CD70 therapy. FCGR3A is almost entirely immune [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.999] and follows the overall immune score [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=0.795], a marker of hot, infiltrated tumours and a control. CD74 and CXCR4 are likewise immune-cell genes whose bulk levels separate hot from cold tumours rather than mark cancer cells.

integration.text: The streams converge most clearly on a HIF-driven tumour-cell programme downstream of VHL loss: CA9, COXFA4L2, NNMT and CD70 are tumour-up in omics, tumour-intrinsic by purity and single-cell data, replicated in TCGA and supported by literature. They disagree on what the genes are for. Literature and drug history make CA9 and CD70 surface targets, Open Targets gives CD70, COXFA4L2 and NNMT only weak prior association, and DepMap shows no dependency for any of them, so these are best pursued as antigens for antibodies, conjugates, radioligands or cell therapy, not as inhibitor targets. SCARB1 and PIGR show the reverse gap: strong omics and genetic support with no literature in this corpus.

Taken together, the candidates sort into three groups. Targets: CA9, CD70, ENPP3 and SCARB1 as surface antigens, EPAS1 as the one validated dependency, and KDR as a microenvironment target on endothelium. Biomarkers: PSAT1, PCK1, ALDOB, UMOD and SLC22A8 as tumour-down markers of lost tubule identity, and NNMT as a tumour-up prognostic marker that is also small-molecule tractable. Mechanism: VHL and PBRM1, the recurrent drivers that explain the programme and stratify patients but cannot be inhibited.

targets.rationale: First in the overall ranking and robust in the target profile; tumour-intrinsic in bulk, single-cell and spatial data, replicated in TCGA, with girentuximab antibody and imaging agents in the clinic. No ccRCC dependency, so its value is as a surface antigen and imaging biomarker.

Robust in the target profile, membrane protein up in tumour, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, with the highest conjugate suitability among controls and anti-CD70 agents in early trials. Placed below CA9 because immune cells contribute much of its RNA and normal-tissue staining data were missing.

Tumour-up and tumour-intrinsic, with RCC-cell attribution in two single-cell datasets, protein replication in the confirmatory cohort and an adverse survival association in TCGA; small-molecule tractable. Ranked high because it is the best replicated tumour-up gene, although DepMap shows no dependency.
The established ccRCC target of belzutifan and the only reviewed gene with a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap; included as the reference target rather than a new finding.

First and most robust in the target profile, protein up in tumour and replicated in the confirmatory cohort, with genetic support in Open Targets. Placed below CA9 and CD70 because it has no drugs, no dependency, no literature in this corpus and heterogeneous tumour-cell expression with adrenal staining.
The most robust biomarker call: down in tumour at RNA and protein, replicated in TCGA and in the confirmatory cohort, with low expression linked to worse prognosis. A biomarker, not a target.
Robust second in the biomarker profile, with protein and both shared phosphosites replicating as lower in the confirmatory cohort; its subtype link is RNA-level only.

Surface enzyme up in tumour and tumour-intrinsic, robust in the target profile, with the conjugate AGS-16C3F as precedent. Ranked after SCARB1 because it stains normal kidney, an on-target toxicity concern.

Among the strongest down-regulated genes, replicated in TCGA with a prognostic association and literature support, marking loss of proximal-tubule identity. Placed below PSAT1 and PCK1 because its biomarker rank depends on the weights.

Exploratory: the leading tumour-track discovery candidate, made by RCC cells, protein up in tumour, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, with few ccRCC papers and no drug. Main limitation: surface localisation, normal-tissue staining and dependency are unknown, and only a minority of RCC cells express it.
Approved anti-angiogenic target, expressed by endothelium in single-cell and spatial data with no tumour-cell contribution or cell-line dependency; included as a microenvironment target and control.

Robust in the target profile, the MCT4 lactate exporter is up in tumour at RNA, protein and phospho. Placed low because its cell of origin does not replicate between single-cell datasets and it has no dependency.

Robust top-ten in the overall ranking and supported by preclinical literature as a HIF-induced mitochondrial gene linked to CA9, but with weak Open Targets association, non-specific drugs and no dependency, so it is a biomarker and mechanism lead more than a target.

Exploratory: second tumour-track discovery candidate, mostly in RCC cells, protein up in tumour, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust. Main limitation: an intracellular GTPase with no functional or dependency evidence and a sizeable macrophage share.

limitations.text: Bulk CPTAC tissue mixes tumour, stroma and immune cells; purity extrapolation and single-cell attribution reduce but do not remove infiltration artefacts, and the single-cell datasets have few donors.
No candidate other than EPAS1 shows a selective DepMap dependency, so most target calls rest on surface location, tumour specificity and existing drugs rather than on demonstrated essentiality.

The literature corpus is a few hundred ccRCC abstracts, so missing literature (SCARB1, PIGR, the discovery genes) means missing from this corpus, not absent from the field. Most prognostic literature comes from single bioinformatic or small IHC studies.
Convergence and profile scores are deterministic rankings with weight-sensitivity intervals, not statistical tests; positions outside the robust core depend on the chosen weights.
Treatment-response results come from trial arms of about ninety patients or from a very small nivolumab trial; none differs between arms after correction, and they are associations, not predictors.
ADC suitability and structural-context scores are descriptive heuristics; they do not show that a conjugate, radioligand or degrader would work, and CD70 lacked normal-tissue staining data.

Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses prioritised for experimental validation; none has been tested functionally here, and the analysis does not show that treating any gene would benefit patients. Passing the automatic checks is not complete scientific validation.
Some layers were not covered within the agents' tool budgets, including STRING interactions, ADC and immune profiles for the tumour-down biomarkers, and single-cell values for CD70.
